seat.BEST_WHY:
The wall run along y≈428–450, x≈190–500. It is a horizontal timber laid over stone with vertical pins driven through it, and the pins are not on a rhythm — measuring left to right the gaps come out roughly 40, 62, 28, 55, 48px, and two of them (x≈355, x≈490) are noticeably fatter than the rest. One pin at x≈420 stops short of the timber's lower edge; the one at x≈490 overshoots it. That's a run somebody built rather than tiled. Underneath it there is a genuine terminating shadow at y≈456 (sampled value 23 against a floor at 85 immediately below), so the wall keeps a footprint instead of dissolving.

Second thing, the floor right of the player: at native resolution there is a large scribed arc crossing four separate flagstones between x≈250–500, y≈250–290 (art px) — a single mark that ignores the joint grid. Wear that spans tiles is the hardest thing to fake and the fastest tell that the floor is a surface and not a tileset. The joints themselves vary: the run below the player has joints that go dark-thin, dark-thick, then almost vanish across three stones in a row, so the stones read as cut and settled rather than stamped.

Third, the corridor at x≈500–560, y≈180–420: cables strung diagonally with pins at the anchor points, a pale rectangle at y≈300–340 carrying faint grey stroke-marks that reads as a pinned notice, and a small hanging object at y≈365. It is dressed, and dressed with the specific vocabulary of rope and driven pins.
seat.WORST_WHY:
Four things, any one of which is disqualifying.

The mud field is one 48×48px block stamped across the entire 190×288px area. I measured it: horizontal self-difference at a 48px offset drops to 5.04 against 7.2–7.6 at every other pitch; vertical the same, 8.83 at 48 against 9.4–11.5. That is roughly two dozen repeats of the identical dark-red branching mottle, and the seams are visible by eye in the upper mud around x≈100–200, y≈40–140 — the same three-pronged red fork recurs on a lattice.

There is no light model at all. The brief says the picture darkens away from the figure. This frame is uniformly lit corner to corner; the stone at x≈360, y≈270 is the same value as the stone at x≈20, y≈20. Nothing anywhere falls off.

The terrain boundaries are dead-straight full-height tile-column seams: mud meets water at exactly x=247, water meets stone at exactly x=343, stone meets mud at x=54. No bank, no wet margin, no spill, no debris. A water body with a ruled edge.

The two chests at x≈64–96, y≈4–36 and y≈48–80 are drawn in three-quarter perspective — you can see the vertical front planks of a box receding below the lid — and dropped into a straight top-down frame. They also cast soft drop shadows onto the mud below them, and they and the green figure's black ellipse are the only shadows in the image; nothing else casts anything.

Minor but of a piece: the teal moss blob at x≈18, y≈150 is the same asset, mirrored, as the one at x≈355, y≈150. The white scatter at x≈215, y≈118 is ten unstructured white pixels that resolve into no object.

flip_list: The middle prop at x≈408, y≈613 is not readable as an object. At native resolution it is a lumpy heart-shaped mass of saturated red-orange with loose yellow pixels along its lower edge — no straight plank edges, no consistent light direction, and it is the highest-chroma element in the entire frame. Redraw it with the same two-plank construction and the same silhouette discipline as the prop at x≈285, or cut it.

Those three props sit at y≈612, 613, 613, spaced 125px and 125px apart, and are three different sizes and three different colour temperatures of the same crossed-plank object. Break the row: move at least one off that y, and settle on one plank width and one wood hue across all three.

The round object at x≈597, y≈548 contains a lit flame and emits no light. The cobbles of its own ring, 1–2px from the flame, sit at the same value as unlit stones 30px away. Either give it a local falloff that brightens the surrounding four or five flagstones, or take the flame out.
That same object's interior is near-pure black with a hard edge; every other dark in the lit floor is a warm brown. Re-key the hole interior to the frame's darkest warm brown.
Its ring cobbles read brighter than floor stones that are closer to the player's lamp. Re-light the prop through the same distance falloff as the floor instead of drawing it at fixed value.
The flame inside it is four flat colour steps at ~10px tall — an interface-icon rendering. Redraw at the scene's material fidelity or remove.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
item_exit.item: #202 - the top-to-face turn: the worn arris, built in the traffic-modulated form WALL-RECIPE.md 4.1 said was the only adoptable one
item_exit.claim: face and top read as separate objects because the only thing at the turn is a dark line, and a dark line separates. The bar draws a pale worn edge there. It was refused as a UNIFORM band and is adoptable modulated by traffic, which the face family's four-step age index now supplies
item_exit.measured: PRESENT AND NON-UNIFORM: 992 pixels change against the previous gated frame (sha b347247f, r002-props), in 2-device-row runs at the turns and nowhere else; ages 2-3 only, 11 of 24 reveals in this scene, clustered on the spine (...11233.22110...) and absent on the quiet branches. AMPLITUDE, authored: 1.30x and 1.45x the cap's own top value, Weber +0.3000 and +0.4500, both inside the bar's measured 1.27-1.47 and both clear of 13.8's 0.1440. DELIVERED, worst cell reported: lit wall cap 75.83 -> arris 113.33, ratio 1.495; DIM WALL cap 25.58 -> arris 44.20, ratio 1.728 - over the bar's band, and the 6.3 exposure, stated for the gate. Zero blown pixels in either (0 of 532, 0 of 300), so 183's 'never blown' holds. The turn now profiles cap 75.8 -> arris 113.3 -> shadowed underside 25.0 -> face 59.0 where it was 75.8 -> 24.8 -> 59.0.

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.

dispositions.measured: THIS ONE IS MINE AND IT IS NOT A PROP FAULT. I placed the barricade family at (4,14), (6,14) and (8,14) - one row, constant pitch, which at 64px is the 125px spacing the seat measured. That is 8.3.1's motif trap built by the SCENE rather than by a tile: a repeated element at constant pitch reads as pattern, and the fix is arrangement, not art. The second half - one plank width, one hue - is #204's tint snap plus the family's missing fourth variant.
